name: Opus 5 trend following
strategy: Systematic time-series trend with signals refreshed through the 2026-10-23 close: long only where price is above both the 50- and 200-day moving average with positive 3-month momentum, short only where both are broken and momentum is negative, flat otherwise - now holding only the surviving energy-shock legs (XLE, USO) and the dollar (UUP), with the duration, housing, crypto and equity sleeves flat in cash because their signals no longer qualify.
reassessment_note: I refreshed the signals from Yahoo daily closes through 10-23. The book's own entry rules now fail on three sleeves. TLT closed at 81.34, above its 50-DMA of 80.56 (it is still below the 200-DMA of 84.78), so the short no longer has both averages broken, and 1-month momentum is +2.4%. ITB closed at 90.57, above its 50-DMA of 90.38 (still below the 200-DMA of 96.46); it rallied 6.6% against the short this week and 1-month momentum is +2.6%. BTC closed at 81,074, below its 50-DMA of 81,778, with 1-month momentum of -3.9%, so the long no longer has price above both averages. A rules-based trend book that keeps legs after their rules stop qualifying is just holding a view, so I exit all three; the round trip costs only a few basis points. XLE, USO and UUP still pass the long rule cleanly (XLE 69.33 vs 64.34 / 58.18 with 3m +18.8%; USO 169.53 vs 146.47 / 121.61 with 3m +35.9%; UUP 28.96 vs 28.48 / 27.88 with 3m +1.3%). I keep them at their existing weights rather than resizing, to avoid churn. SPY stays out: it is below its 50-DMA (759.97 vs 767.81) with 1m -0.9%. The resulting 65% cash earns 4% APY, and that is the honest output of the system right now. Research note: I ran two web searches for this week's macro news and neither returned dated coverage of the week of 10-23, so this decision rests on the price data and the mandate's rules, not on news flow.

positions.thesis: The energy sleeve is the cleanest trend in the book: 69.33 is 7.8% above the 50-DMA and 19% above the 200-DMA, with 3m momentum of +18.8% and 1m of +10.8%. At 20% weight with about 20% realised vol, it is the largest risk-adjusted leg. The 18% stop sits roughly below the 50-DMA region, so it only fires if the trend actually breaks.

Crude, the source of the energy-shock macro trend, is the strongest signal in the universe: 169.53 against a 50-DMA of 146.47 and a 200-DMA of 121.61, with 3m momentum of +35.9%. It is sized at only 9% because realised vol is about 32%, which keeps its risk contribution similar to XLE. The 15% stop and 35% take-profit are kept from the existing leg to bank a blow-off.

The dollar still qualifies as a long: 28.96 is above the 50-DMA of 28.48 and the 200-DMA of 27.88, with 3m momentum of +1.3%. It is the weakest of the three surviving trends, so I keep it at its existing small 6% weight; at about 5% realised vol it barely moves book risk. The tight 6% stop exits if the dollar trend reverses.
